entries.title: Exodus 30:1
segments: In the Mosaic ritual we are continually reminded of the priesthood, sacrifice, and intercession of Christ, through the incense of whose merits alone our prayers can ascend with acceptance before God.

entries.title: Exodus 30:3
segments: A crown; cornice or border.

entries.title: Exodus 30:6
segments: The veil; which separated the holy from the most holy place, so that the altar stood directly over against the ark of the covenant, being separated from it by the veil.

entries.title: Exodus 30:7
segments: Sweet incense; this represented the prayers of God's people made acceptable by the intercession of Christ,
, as the burnt-offering did his atonement.

entries.title: Exodus 30:8
segments: Our need of Christ's intercession is constant; and day by day, morning and evening, continually our supplications should ascend before him as incense, and the lifting up of our hearts in prayer and praise as our habitual sacrifice.

entries.title: Exodus 30:9
segments: Strange incense; other than that prescribed,

entries.title: Exodus 30:10
segments: Once in a year; on the great day of atonement.
Shall--make atonement; this showed that atonement was necessary, in order to the efficacy of intercession.

entries.title: Exodus 30:12
segments:
The sum; the census; their number. 
 
  A ransom for his soul; a tribute paid to God for the preservation and blessings of life, and for the support of divine worship.

entries.title: Exodus 30:13
segments: Half a shekel; in value about twenty-five cents.

entries.title: Exodus 30:15
segments: Not give more--not give less; teaching that before God the rich and poor are of equal worth, and equally need the same atonement.

entries.title: Exodus 30:16
segments: That it may be a memorial unto the children of Israel; more literally, "that it may be to the children of Israel for a memorial before the Lord;" that is, that it may remind God in their behalf,

, of the ransom they have paid for their souls. 
 
  To make an atonement for your souls; so that God shall send no plague among them.

A portion of what God has given us should be gratefully devoted to the support of his worship, as a memorial of his goodness and a testimony of our obligations for all the blessings of his providence and grace.

entries.title: Exodus 30:18
segments: A laver; large bowl or basin.

entries.title: Exodus 30:20
segments: Wash with water; an emblem of the purifying influences of the Holy Ghost.

entries.title: Exodus 30:21
segments: Purity of heart and life is as needful as the pardon of sin; and for it we should look habitually to the Holy Spirit, the Author and Finisher of all that is spiritually good in the children of men.

entries.title: Exodus 30:23
segments:
Principal spices; of the purest and most precious kind. 
 
  Five hundred shekels; the shekel has been estimated at from ten to ten and three quarters pennyweights.  Five hundered shekels would then be from about nineteen to twenty-two and a third pounds, troy weight; or, from a little less than sixteen, to about eighteen and a half pounds avoirdupois.

entries.title: Exodus 30:25
segments: The apothecary; perfumer, or maker of ointments.

entries.title: Exodus 30:30
segments: Anoint Aaron and his sons; in token of the necessity of their being endued with the Holy Spirit, to fit them for their duties.

entries.title: Exodus 30:31
segments: All our services must be perfumed with the incense of Christ's merits, and be the fruit of his Spirit, working in us both to will and also to do, in order to be holy, or ascend before God with acceptance.

entries.title: Exodus 30:32
segments: Upon man's flesh; the flesh of men who were not priests.

entries.title: Exodus 30:34
segments: Stacte--onycha, and galbanum; fragrant spices or gums.  Some, however, suppose onycha to be a species of shell which, when burnt, yields a strong odor.

entries.title: Exodus 30:35
segments: Confection; mixture, to burn on the altar of incense.

entries.title: Exodus 30:38
segments: While we rely on the atonement, righteousness, and intercession of Christ as the one only and all-sufficient Mediator, and look to his Spirit as the only Sanctifier, we should most carefully abstain from looking to or depending on any other; for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
